raw_text:
- Understanding completion-time differences in sites with identical nominal work processes

Assumptions
- Differences in completion times can be explained by measurable factors

Research design
- Bayesian framework with prior beliefs about common factors affecting completion times

Data or evidence needed
- Completion times and observed work process factors (e.g., employee efficiency, workload)
- Observational data on external conditions (e.g., task complexity, time pressure)

Measurement
- Binary indicators for the presence of measurable work process factors
- Continuous measures of external conditions affecting task completion

Analysis
- Bayesian regression analysis to model completion times as a function of work process factors and external conditions
- Sensitivity analysis to investigate the relative importance of different factors

Decision / stopping rule
- Setting decision thresholds for the acceptance or rejection of competing explanations based on Bayesian credible intervals

Limitations
- Data limitations (e.g., missing or noisy data)
- Challenges in accurately measuring work process factors and external conditions
